name: Mount Sharp Boxwork Network
formation_mechanism: Boxwork structures originate when tectonic or compaction stresses create an interconnected fracture web in lacustrine mudstone bedforms. Mineral-rich groundwater circulates through these open joints, precipitating resistant cements (calcium/magnesium sulfates, iron oxides, or silica). Subsequent eolian deflation strips away the softer intervening host rocks, exhuming the hard mineralized veins as blade-like standing walls.
significance: Documents persistent late-stage subsurface groundwater circulation occurring long after surface lakes dried out in Gale Crater. Demonstrates localized habitability niches protected from surface radiation.
hypotheses: Groundwater circulation driven by regional thermal gradient or remnant impact heat.
Mineral veins precipitated during late-stage evaporation of sulfate-saturated pore fluids.
Veins represent multiple distinct fluid pulses with varying geochemical compositions.
sampling_protocols: Document ridge strike, dip, and polygonal cell dimensions with high-resolution stereo mast photography.
Extract rock core samples from both the resistant blade fill and the adjacent host mudstone for isotopic comparison.
Conduct in-situ alpha particle X-ray spectrometry (APXS) and Raman spectroscopy for sulfur, magnesium, and hydration bonds.
